name: Per-user cloud computer
summary: Each user, or each agent, gets its own long-lived virtual machine in the cloud that keeps its files, installed tools and running processes between sessions. The agent can keep working while the user's laptop is closed, and the user can come back to the same environment later.
how: Create one VM or persistent sandbox per user or agent
Install tools and keep state on its disk
Pause or stop it when idle, resume on the next task
Connect to it from chat, web or a local client
facts: Persistent sandboxes such as Daytona, Vercel Sandbox, Docker Cloud Sandboxes
Disk, and often memory, survive between sessions
Agent keeps context and setup, but you pay for idle storage and must secure a long-lived machine
goodFor: Agents that accumulate tools and files over time
watchOut: State drift: a long-lived machine collects junk and secrets
Storage, and on some providers compute, is billed while idle
